input.scenario:
Theme: You already count every small spend, so KITE pays some of it back: 5% on groceries, transport and coffee, cent by cent.
Scenes: 4 · 8 s

1. HOOK (0.0–2.4 s): "€1.80 for milk." then "+9¢ back." Someone buys an ordinary carton of milk, and a little money comes straight back before they've left the checkout.

2. PROOF (2.4–4.6 s): "Tram €3.20 · +16¢" then "Flat white €3.60 · +18¢". The day goes on with the ride home and the morning coffee, and each small spend pays back as it happens.

3. TALLY (4.6–5.6 s): "Today: 43¢ back." The three everyday spends add up to one real number the person didn't have to chase.

4. OFFER + CTA (5.6–8 s): "Free card. 3 minutes / no fee · no minimum" · CTA "GET THE CARD". Fully resolved by 6.8 s, then holds with the brand and CTA readable until 8 s.

styles.name: Split Ledger
styles.idea: Documentary footage of the real KITE card at the checkout, in a tote on the tram and tapping a café terminal, seen through split panels cut into the flat orange field, while the brand tab carries each cent back up into cream plaques.
styles.direction: MEDIUM: the brand's native system pushed to its sharpest form, with live documentary video (KITE_warm_v1 LUT at 80%, grain 3%) in split panels set into a flat #FF5A1F field. HERO: the KITE card in a real hand in each world (supplied supermarket.mp4, tram.mp4 and cafe.mp4, reframed so no faces show; the cashier in supermarket.mp4 is cropped out above the shoulder line). COMPOSITION (1:1 master): the field takes the top 44% and the video panel the bottom 56%. The corner wordmark is the supplied SVG in cream, 23.5u wide, at 108/68 px, and never moves. Copy sits in a block anchored 38 px above the split line, so it rides with the line when the line moves. In 9:16 the field is at the top and the video runs to the bottom edge. In 16:9 the video becomes a right-hand column. TYPE: Schibsted Grotesk 800. The hook is 83 px and list lines are 62–64 px. Each line sits on its own cream plaque with orange text, radius 0 and height 1.08em, using the brand pad. ACCENT DEVICE: the brand tab, a 480×48 px tongue of field poking into the panel with a 16 px outer radius. Exactly one sits on each split, and it alternates sides each beat. It works as the 'return slot' the cents come back through. RECURRING ELEMENT: the plaque stack, which grows one line per spend. MOTION (curves: in = cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), out = cubic-bezier(.55,0,1,.45); no zoom, blur or dissolve; the logo and settled plaques never animate). HOOK 0.00–2.40: frame 0 is already complete. The checkout clip plays, the tab is visible and '€1.80 for milk.' sits on its plaque. At 1.10 the plaque for '+9¢ back.' draws in from the left (scaleX 0→1, 0.20 s) and its text types on by word, 0.125 s per word. The clip's own handheld breathing keeps the frame alive. PROOF 2.40–4.60: at 2.40 the panel leaves through its outer edge (0.16 s, out curve) and the tab goes on the first exit frame. Then 0.04 s of field only with a hard text swap. At 2.60 the tram panel enters from the left (0.25 s, in curve), and 0.05 s after it settles the tab appears. 'Tram €3.20 · +16¢' draws in at 2.70. At 3.50 the café panel slides in from the right over half the split, the tram shot keeps playing in the left half, an 8 px gutter of field separates the two, and the tab jumps to the café side. 'Flat white €3.60 · +18¢' draws in below the first plaque at 3.60. Both stay up until 4.60, so each reads twice. TALLY 4.60–5.60: both panels exit through their outer edges (0.16 s) and the field takes the frame. The three cent figures collapse into one plaque line, 'Today: 43¢ back.', and the 43 counts up 0→43 over 0.45 s in tabular figures. OFFER + CTA 5.60–8.00: the end frame follows the brand layout exactly. The corner logo cuts out on a hard swap. The centred KITE wordmark (47u wide) drops 5u in 0.15 s. 'Free card. 3 minutes / no fee · no minimum' types on from 5.60 at 0.125 s per word, with the last word at 6.48. At 6.55 the CTA plaque 'GET THE CARD' and the official App Store and Google Play badges rise 8u in 0.20 s, settling at 6.75. Hold until 8.00.

styles.name: Cent Odometer
styles.idea: No footage at all: the orange field becomes a running receipt, where each spend prints as a ledger row, the cents stack into a sum column, and a huge tabular 43¢ rolls up like an odometer.
styles.direction: MEDIUM: pure kinetic typography and ledger UI in a field_full composition (a layout the guide allows), with two colours only: cream on #FF5A1F. It reads like the KITE app's activity feed turned into a poster. HERO: the money itself as type, with a giant tabular-figure cent number about 440 px high (cap height around 30% of the short side) that bleeds close to the right margin. COMPOSITION (1:1): the corner wordmark sits at 108/68. On the right is the sum column: row labels in plain cream type at 54 px, right-aligned against cream plaques holding the cents (+9¢, +16¢, +18¢) at 54 px, with an 8 px cream rule underneath. That is literally column addition. The result runs left-aligned on the margin: a 'Today:' plaque, the giant 43¢, then a 'back.' plaque. In 9:16 the column sits above the number inside the safe zone. In 16:9 the column moves to the right third and the number to the left two-thirds. TYPE: Schibsted Grotesk 800 throughout. The headline is 83 px, the ledger rows are 54 px (never smaller, per the brand's 5u floor) and the number is set with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. ACCENT DEVICE: cream plaques with radius 0, one per line, and the 8 px sum rule. RECURRING ELEMENT: the ledger stack. It is born in the HOOK, grows in PROOF and becomes the sum in TALLY, so the spot plays as one continuous receipt feed. MOTION MECHANISM: receipt feed plus odometer drums. Each new row pushes the stack up by one row pitch (a move, 0.25 s, in curve), and the digits roll vertically inside clipped windows. No zoom or blur; the logo and settled plaques never move. HOOK 0.00–2.40: frame 0 already shows '€1.80 for milk.' at headline size on plaques, with a large '+9¢' ghost-row window already open. At 0.90 the drum rolls 0→9 (0.45 s, in curve, digits clipped) and 'back.' types on at 1.40. PROOF 2.40–4.60: hard text swap at 2.40. The hook compresses into ledger row 1 ('Milk  +9¢'), and the stack feeds up to make room for 'Tram €3.20 · +16¢' at the headline line. Its plaque draws in from the left (0.20 s) and the 16 rolls on its drum. At 3.50 the feed pushes again and 'Flat white €3.60 · +18¢' prints the same way. A slow 12 px upward feed between prints keeps the receipt alive. TALLY 4.60–5.60: the three rows snap into the right-hand sum column (move, 0.25 s), and the sum rule draws left to right (0.20 s). The 'Today:' plaque draws in, the giant 43¢ rolls on two drums (the 4 lands at 4.95, the 3 at 5.05, then ¢ cuts on), and 'back.' types on at 5.15. OFFER + CTA 5.60–8.00: the ledger feeds up out of frame (0.16 s, out curve) and the immutable end frame resolves. The centred 47u wordmark drops 5u (0.15 s). The sub-line types on from 5.60 at 0.125 s per word. The 'GET THE CARD' plaque and the official store badges rise 8u at 6.55 and settle by 6.75. Hold until 8.00.

styles.name: Pocket Collage
styles.idea: Photographed cut-out objects from the day (a milk carton, a tram ticket, a flat white seen from above) slap onto the flat orange field one after another, while a flat cream tote pocket at the bottom slowly releases the real KITE card a little more with every cent.
styles.direction: MEDIUM: a top-down photo collage. Real studio photographs of everyday props are shot overhead in soft, even window light (5600K warmed to the LUT) and cut out with hard edges. They sit directly on the flat #FF5A1F field with no drop shadows, no outlines and no paper texture, as the guide requires. Props carry no brands and no readable print: the milk carton is plain white with a muted grey-blue band, the tram ticket is off-white with abstract printed bars, and the flat white is in a white ceramic cup on a saucer with a rosetta in the crema. HERO: one oversized prop per beat, cropped boldly so it bleeds off an edge (the cup fills the right half in PROOF). ACCENT DEVICE: the brand tab reinterpreted as its own metaphor. A flat cream tote with a stitched pocket mouth (a 5 px orange rule) sits at the lower left, and the KITE card pokes out of it. The card follows the reference exactly: a vertical matte orange card with rounded corners, a light-gold chip centred in the upper third, the contactless icon to the right and the cream KITE mark at the bottom (hidden in the pocket until the end). The cream tote gives the orange card the contrast it needs against the field. RECURRING ELEMENT: the card in the pocket. It rises about 20 px with each cent earned, so by TALLY the chip is fully clear. COMPOSITION (1:1): the corner wordmark sits at 108/68. Copy plaques run along the top-left margin (cream plaques, orange text, Schibsted Grotesk 800 at 62–83 px, radius 0). Props occupy the right and centre, and the pocket is anchored bottom-left. In 9:16 the pocket sits above the bottom safe zone; in 16:9 the props line up left to right like the day's timeline. MOTION MECHANISM: stop-motion placement. Each prop drops onto the field with one back.out(1.6) settle, or 'drop' on the brand in curve (0.25 s). It is rotated at most ±4° and held on 12-fps stepped frames for a handmade cadence, while the type stays at 24 fps with the brand curves. The previous prop is shoved off the nearest edge (a move, 0.16 s, out curve), so it reads as a table being cleared, not a slide swap. Constant life comes from a 10 px drift of the hero prop along one axis; no scaling. HOOK 0.00–2.40: frame 0 shows the milk carton large and bleeding off the right edge, the pocket with the card's top edge just showing, and '€1.80 for milk.' on its plaque. At 1.10 the '+9¢ back.' plaque draws in from the left (0.20 s), the text types on by word and the card nudges up 20 px. PROOF 2.40–4.60: the carton is shoved up and out the top-right (it still peeks in the keyframe). The tram ticket drops in tilted −4° at 2.50, and 'Tram €3.20 · +16¢' draws in at 2.65 as the card rises again. At 3.45 the flat white lands as the beat's single weighted settle, overlapping the ticket. 'Flat white €3.60 · +18¢' draws in below at 3.55 and the card rises a third time, showing the full chip and contactless. TALLY 4.60–5.60: the three props slide together into a tidy row along the top (move, 0.25 s), and the 'Today: 43¢ back.' plaque draws in with the 43 counting up in tabular figures. The card reaches its highest point. OFFER + CTA 5.60–8.00: the props and tote exit downward (0.16 s, out curve) and the immutable end frame takes over. The 47u wordmark drops 5u (0.15 s), the sub-line types on from 5.60 at 0.125 s per word, and the 'GET THE CARD' plaque and official store badges rise 8u at 6.55 and settle by 6.75. Hold until 8.00.
